title: Surasa
hook: the gods decide to test Hanuman, and they send the mother of serpents with her mouth wide open
carry: every time he gets bigger, she gets bigger

segments.voice: Yesterday: Mainaka, the winged mountain the wind once saved, repaying his debt to the wind's son.

A coach who keeps raising the bar every time you clear it. Some tests aren't trying to stop you; they're trying to see what you do when force won't work. Over the open sea, Mainaka behind him, Hanuman flies straight into one of those. And the ones who set it up aren't his enemies. They're the gods, who want to know what this monkey is really made of.
screen: `THE BAR KEEPS RISING.` → `THE GODS SET THE TEST.`

segments.voice: The gods, the celestial musicians and the great sages talk it over. They ask Surasa, the mother of the nagas, the serpent beings, to take a terrifying form and block Hanuman's way, so they can see his strength and his cleverness. Surasa rises from the sea huge and frightening: the gods have given you to me as food, she says. You have to enter my mouth. Hanuman doesn't attack. He talks. Briefly and honestly he tells her who he is and why he's here: Rama, the forest, Sita taken, the search. He asks her to let him pass. Then he makes a remarkable offer. Let me find Sita and tell Rama, and I promise I'll come back and enter your mouth. The errand comes first; his own life can wait in line behind it. Surasa refuses. She has a boon, she says, that no one can get past her. And she opens her mouth. So Hanuman grows to ten yojanas, too big to swallow. She opens wider, twenty. He grows to thirty; she opens to forty. On they go, each matching the other, until her mouth gapes a hundred yojanas wide, as wide as the sea he's crossing. Every time he gets bigger, she gets bigger. Force won't settle this. Hanuman, hovering there, has to think of something else.
screen: `THE GODS ASK SURASA TO TEST HIM.` · `HANUMAN TALKS FIRST.` · `I'LL COME BACK, I PROMISE.` · then, large: `HE GROWS; SHE GROWS.`

segments.voice: Let the shoulders drop and bring to mind a situation where pushing harder keeps making it worse, an argument that escalates or a problem that grows each time you force it. For this sit, stop pushing. Let the breath get smaller and slower rather than bigger, and rest in not escalating.
Surasa. The mother of serpents, sent by the gods to test Hanuman, whose mouth grows wider every time he grows bigger, until force can't win.
Your line: every time he gets bigger, she gets bigger. His answer comes tomorrow. Day six hundred eight, done.

howItsDone: Storytellers telling the Sundara Kanda often pause on Surasa's growing mouth before revealing how Hanuman gets through.

original.note: Sanskrit surasā, the name of the mother of the nāgas in this story.

trapdoor: what you thought: Surasa is just another monster.
what it means: she's a test set by the gods to see Hanuman's strength and cleverness.
what a scholar hears: Valmiki frames the episode as a trial of Hanuman's qualities, and later tellings often read the three sea meetings (Mainaka, Surasa, Simhika) as a set.
recall: the harsh rakshasa lord of Janasthana

chat.says: Why didn't Hanuman just fight Surasa? He's strong enough.

chat.meaning: The gods sent Surasa to test his strength and cleverness. Her mouth grew whenever he grew, so force could not win.

Surasa.meaning: mother of the serpent beings, sent by the gods to test Hanuman

Mainaka.meaning: the golden mountain that rose from the sea to offer rest

yojanas.meaning: an old Indian measure of distance, many miles each

Sita.meaning: Rama's wife, carried off to Lanka by Ravana

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Sundara Kanda 1 (the gods ask Surasa to test Hanuman; the contest of growing)
